issue.title: Upload fails for videos larger than 2 GB
issue.author: mira-dev

summary.headline: Uploads over 2 GB fail because the file size is stored in a 32-bit integer
summary.tldr: Any file larger than 2,147,483,647 bytes overflows `ChunkPlan.totalSize`, so the uploader asks for a negative number of chunks and the server rejects the session with HTTP 400. Fixed in PR #151 by switching to `int64`; a regression test with a sparse 3 GB file was added.

nodes.title: Uploading a 2.4 GB video fails at 0%
nodes.detail: The reporter shared a phone video. The progress bar never moves and the app shows "Upload failed, try again". Smaller videos from the same phone upload fine.

nodes.title: Android and desktop, v3.8.0 and later
nodes.detail: Three other users confirm the problem on Android 15 and on the Windows desktop client. Nobody can reproduce it on v3.7.

nodes.title: Server answers HTTP 400 "chunk_count must be positive"
nodes.detail: The debug log shows the client's create-session request with `chunk_count: -1048`. The server rejects it before any bytes are sent.

nodes.title: Proxy or CDN times out on long uploads
nodes.detail: First guess from a maintainer: large uploads hit the 60 s proxy timeout.

nodes.title: Fails instantly, before any data is sent
nodes.detail: The failure happens within 200 ms at 0 bytes transferred, so a timeout on a long transfer cannot be the cause.

nodes.title: File size overflows a 32-bit integer
nodes.detail: A negative chunk count for a file just over 2 GB points at signed 32-bit overflow: 2.4 GB wraps to a negative number.

nodes.title: Bisected to the chunk-planner refactor in v3.8.0
nodes.detail: `git bisect` between v3.7.2 and v3.8.0 lands on commit `a1b2c3d`, "Move chunk planning into ChunkPlan".

nodes.title: ChunkPlan.totalSize is declared as int32
nodes.detail: The refactor copied the size into a new `ChunkPlan` struct whose `totalSize` field is `int32`. The old code used `int64` throughout. Any file of 2^31 bytes or more wraps negative, and `chunkCount = ceil(totalSize / chunkSize)` goes negative with it.

nodes.title: core/upload/chunk_plan.go: totalSize int32
nodes.detail: `type ChunkPlan struct { totalSize int32; chunkSize int32 }`

nodes.title: Downgrade to v3.7.2 or trim the video
nodes.detail: Suggested while the fix was in review.

nodes.title: PR #151: use int64 for sizes in ChunkPlan
nodes.detail: Changes `totalSize` to `int64` and adds a check that rejects a non-positive chunk count with a clear error instead of sending it to the server.

nodes.title: Regression test uploads a sparse 3 GB file
nodes.detail: `TestChunkPlanLargeFile` creates a sparse 3 GB file and checks the chunk count. It fails on v3.8.0 and passes with the fix.

nodes.title: Reporter confirms the 2.4 GB video uploads in v3.8.2

edges.note: Debug logging requested to see the server response
Fails at 0 bytes, so no long transfer is involved
A negative chunk count is the clue

open_questions: Do other structs created in the v3.8.0 refactor also use int32 for byte counts?
next_steps: Audit core/upload for other int32 size fields.
Add a lint rule that flags int32 fields named *Size or *Bytes.

flow.title: What happens when you upload a video from the phone

steps.title: User shares a 2.4 GB video
steps.detail: The share sheet hands the file to `UploadWorker`, which calls the shared upload core.

steps.title: Start upload, read file size
steps.detail: `Start` stats the file (2,576,980,378 bytes) and builds a `ChunkPlan` from the size.

steps.title: Size kept as int64
steps.detail: What PR #151 changes: `totalSize` is an `int64`, so a 2.4 GB size stays positive.

steps.title: Size stored in a 32-bit int
steps.detail: The v3.8.0 refactor moved chunk planning into `ChunkPlan` and declared `totalSize` as `int32`. Any file of 2^31 bytes or more wraps to a negative number here.

fix.label: PR #151: use int64
fix.detail: Changes `totalSize` to `int64` and rejects a non-positive chunk count before calling the server.

steps.title: Chunk count comes out negative
steps.detail: With a negative `totalSize`, `chunkCount` is -1048 for the reporter's file. Nothing checks it.

steps.title: Server rejects the upload session
steps.detail: `POST /sessions` with `chunk_count: -1048` fails validation: HTTP 400 "chunk_count must be positive".

steps.title: "Upload failed, try again" at 0%
steps.detail: The worker shows a generic error for any failed session, so the reporter never sees the 400 message.

cases.title: 2.4 GB video
cases.should: The size stays positive and the upload completes
cases.does: `totalSize` wraps negative; the server rejects the session with HTTP 400

background.context: The photo-sync app uploads a video in chunks. The upload core plans the upload from the file size, `ChunkPlan`, then asks the Sync API to open an upload session with the number of chunks. The server only accepts a positive chunk count.
background.rule: Byte counts must be stored in 64-bit integers: a phone video can be larger than 2,147,483,647 bytes, the largest value an `int32` holds.

terms.meaning: Struct in core/upload that holds the file size and how it is split into chunks.
32-bit signed integer; values above 2,147,483,647 wrap around to negative numbers.
Server-side record created by `POST /sessions` before any chunk is sent.
